hooks.text: NASA is dropping a titanium beach ball into a 900-degree hellscape.
Can a titanium sphere survive the crushing pressure of a lost ocean?
One titanium sphere will dive through 900 degrees to find an ocean.

title: NASA's titanium probe to Venus
description: NASA is dropping a specialized titanium sphere into the 900-degree atmosphere of Venus to find evidence of ancient oceans.

beats.text: NASA is dropping a titanium beach ball into a 900-degree hellscape.
beats.visual: artist concept of the DAVINCI descent probe dropping through Venus clouds, 2021

beats.text: Venus features a surface hot enough to melt lead and crushing pressure ninety times greater than Earth's.
beats.visual: color panorama of the surface of Venus from the Soviet Venera 14 lander, 1982

beats.text: In 2021, NASA selected the DAVINCI mission to pierce the planet's toxic clouds of sulfuric acid.
beats.visual: photograph of the NASA Goddard Space Flight Center sign and facility, 2021
queries: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center sign

beats.text: The heart of the mission is a titanium sphere built to survive a one-hour plunge through the crushing air.
beats.visual: artist illustration of the DAVINCI spherical descent probe hardware, 2021

beats.text: This descent probe will sniff noble gases to discover if Earth's twin once held vast water oceans.
beats.visual: artist concept of an ancient Venus with blue oceans and white clouds, 2021

beats.text: Before crashing, the sphere will capture the first high-resolution views of Venus's rugged mountains since 1982.
beats.visual: radar map of Venus's rugged tesserae terrain from the Magellan spacecraft, 1991

beats.text: Named after Leonardo da Vinci, this is NASA's first atmospheric entry into Venus since the 1970s.
beats.visual: historical drawing of the aerial screw by Leonardo da Vinci, 1489

beats.text: It is a daring, high-stakes journey into a 900-degree hellscape.
beats.visual: artist concept of the DAVINCI probe falling toward the rocky Venusian surface, 2021
